source.title: XXX Spin Chain: from Bethe Solution to Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For the antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg XXX spin chain, correlation functions are known to be expressible as polynomials in ln 2 and in values of the Riemann zeta function at odd arguments, equivalently in the alternating zeta series at odd arguments, with rational coefficients. Find an efficient explicit description of those rational coefficients that appear in these polynomial formulas for the XXX spin-chain correlation functions.

evidence.quote: However we still not have explicit expressions for the rational coefficients that enter in the expression for the correlation functions as polynomials in ln 2 and Riemann zeta function at odd arguments. Such a description will provide a tractable formula for the correlations of the XXX spin chain.

Open problem: Efficient description of the rational coefficients which appear in the expression for the correlation functions of the XXX spin chain as a polynomial in alternating zeta series at odd arguments.

accepted.question_text: Consider the XXZ spin chain with Hamiltonian H_XXZ in the gapped antiferromagnetic regime Δ < -1. In this regime the entropy S(ρ(n)) of a block of n neighboring spins in the ground state is expected to converge, as n becomes large, to a finite limiting value S(∞). Determine analytically this limiting subsystem entropy S(∞) for the XXZ spin chain when the block size tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: In the gapped antiferromagnetic case (∆ < −1) we expect that S(ρ(n)) will tend to a limiting value S(∞) but at this moment the analytic evaluation of this constant is missing.
Open problem: For the XXZ spin chain in the antiferromagnetic region (∆ < −1) calculate the limiting value of the entropy of a subsystem when the number of spins in the block is large.

accepted.question_text: For the XXZ spin chain in the critical regime -1 ≤ Δ < 1, obtain an explicit analytic asymptotic formula for the time- and temperature-dependent correlation functions, such as g(n,t), in the limit of large spatial separation and large time separation. In particular, derive the formula describing their expected exponential decay in this critical region.

evidence.quote: Despite these considerable efforts the asymptotics of time and temperature dependent correlation functions, such as g(n, t) (see 13) for the XXZ spin chain, are still out of our reach. We expect that they will decay exponentially like in the previous examples of the isotropic XY spin chain or the δ-function Bose gas but at this moment we do not have such a result.
Open problem: Derive an explicit analytic formula describing the asymptotic exponential decay of time and temperature correlation functions in the critical region (−1 ≤ ∆ < 1) of the XXZ spin chain.

accepted.question_text: For the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions, compute the correlation functions both in the bulk and at the boundary. The difficulty is that this model lacks translation invariance, although some determinant representations and boundary results are already known near the boundary.

evidence.quote: As in all exactly solvable models the study of correlation functions is of extreme importance. In the case of the six vertex model with DWBC an added difficulty is constituted by the lack of translation invariance.
Open problem: Calculate the bulk and boundary correlation functions of the six vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

accepted.question_text: Generalize domain wall boundary conditions to other exactly solvable models in such a way that the partition function of the resulting model is still given by a determinant whose dimension is proportional to the size of the system, analogously to the determinant formula for the six-vertex model with domain wall boundary conditions.

evidence.quote: The main feature of formula (19) is the fact that the partition function of the six vertex model with DWBC is expressed as a determinant of the size of the system. The next obvious step would be the generalization of DWBC in the case of other models such that the partition function share the same feature.

Open problem: Obtain generalizations of domain wall boundary conditions for other models such that the partition function is expressed as a determinant of a dimension proportional with the size of the system.
